_comment: THE MATERIALS TABLE (docs/plan_crafting_and_materials.md 1). A MATERIAL IS GENERIC: there is no deer_hide, there is Hide. A SOURCE - an animal, a plant, later a deposit - states the characteristics of what IT yields, through the `materials` block on that source's own yield edge, and that edge has the SAME SHAPE on fauna_config.json and flora_config.json. Nothing in this model is fauna- or flora-shaped. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_characteristics: A CHARACTERISTIC VECTOR, NEVER A QUALITY SCALAR. Mammoth hide is toughness excellent / suppleness poor and a hare pelt is the reverse, so those are not two rungs of one ladder: THERE IS NO BEST HIDE, only the right one for the job, and spending the mammoth hide on a basket is a mistake the player is free to make. A single quality number would rank them, name a winner and delete that decision. THE RATING BELONGS TO THE AXIS, NOT TO THE MATERIAL - 'excellent toughness' says the toughness is excellent and makes no claim about the hide, which is what lets ordinary quality words coexist with there being no best hide.
_comment_bands: BANDS ARE CATEGORIES ON SCREEN AND THE MERGE RULE UNDERNEATH. A source states an EXACT reading (toughness 0.55); the panel and the recipes speak in these four rungs. Two arrivals whose per-axis bands all match become ONE batch in the band's store - without that the store grows without bound, one pile of hide per turn hunted. THE EXACT VALUE SURVIVES THE MERGE as the batch's amount-weighted average and is what crafting reads, so two `good` hides are still not interchangeable and a recipe wanting good toughness pays out differently for .58 than for .79. `from` is where a band OPENS; the first must be 0.0 (every reading has to select a band) and the seams must strictly ascend (an equal or descending seam makes a band unreachable). Retuning these rungs re-partitions every batch on the map, which is a bigger change than it looks.
_comment_hand_working: HAND_WORKING IS ONE PROPERTY OF THE MATERIAL, never a prerequisite repeated on every recipe. You can twist cordage by hand and scrape a hide with a sharp rock, so the three organic materials fall back to a bare-handed rate; you CANNOT work metal without heat, so metal will simply OMIT this block - and an absent block means rate 0, which is what refuses the craft with no 'you cannot craft that' branch anywhere, exactly as max(0, attack - defense) refuses a hunt. `quality_ceiling` is the best reading a bare-handed craft can realize (output = min(material reading, ceiling)): fine flax with no loom still makes a standard basket. THE CEILING BELONGS TO THE MATERIAL, NOT TO THE ABSENT TOOL - a tool that is not there cannot declare anything, and one home per fact.
_comment_varieties: VARIETIES ARE NAMING, NOT MATERIALS - named presets over a material's own axes, so an author can write `copper` and a player can read 'Copper' while the material stays one generic thing with one craft and one tool axis. It is also what collapses the metal tech ladder into one mechanism: no separate Bronzeworking and Ironworking, only Smithing plus a furnace whose temperature ceiling decides which varieties are reachable. THE LOADER SUPPORTS THEM AND NOTHING SHIPS ONE: the four organic axes have no presets worth naming, and metal has no producer until the minerals arc, so a variety row here would be visible dead content (the same reason the bronze equipment tier stays out of config). The mechanism is exercised by a test fixture instead.
_comment_roster: EIGHT MATERIALS SHIP: THE THREE ORGANICS, WHICH ARE CRAFTED; THE THREE LUXURY CROPS, WHICH ARE NOT; AND THE TWO THE PEN EATS - WOOD AND HURDLES. Stone, clay and metal still have no producer until the minerals arc lands, and an unreachable material is dead content the whole catalogue publishes. WOOD HAS NO PRODUCER EITHER AND IS REACHABLE ANYWAY, WHICH IS THE ONE THING ON THIS ROSTER TRUE OF NOTHING ELSE: every band is SPAWNED holding some (`start_stock`, a per-worker opening pile seeded by worldgen beside the band's kit), because the hurdles recipe is what a pen is built out of and forest foraging - the producer that will retire the start stock - has its own tracker item. HURDLES ARE A MATERIAL AND WERE AN EQUIPMENT ITEM (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 2.7): the test is whether the thing comes home with you. A hoe goes to the next field, so it is kit - it wears with use and its absence makes the work dearer, never impossible. A fence STAYS IN THE GROUND, so it is material: it is spent, and no number of hands replaces it. THEY DECLARE NO `craft` AND NO `hand_working`, on the luxury crops' shape: `craft` names the craft that works a material as an INPUT, and nothing takes hurdles as an input - they are consumed by an IMPROVEMENT (the `animal:pen` rung's build pile and upkeep rate), not by a bench. NOTHING READS EITHER OF THEIR AXES AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: `stoutness` and `span` exist because RecipeOutput::material and MaterialDef both require a material to be rated, and a quality axis a pen READ would invite 'a better fence contains better' - the containment-scaling that slice deliberately defers. THE THREE LUXURY ROWS ARE THE OTHER DELIBERATE EXCEPTION, AND THEY ARE NOT UNREACHABLE - THEY ARE UNCRAFTED: tobacco, tea and grape each have a producer TODAY (the flora roster's three cash crops, which pay them on every harvest) and no bench, because the craft that would turn a leaf into a cure or a grape into wine does not exist. `craft` is therefore OMITTED on those three, exactly as `hand_working` is omitted one level down for a material nothing bare-handed can work: an absent craft means NOTHING works it, with no 'you cannot craft that' branch anywhere, and crafts_declared_by simply does not list a craft that is not there, so no recipe can name it. THEIR AXES AND EVERY READING BELOW ARE PROVISIONAL PLACEHOLDERS, not tuned values: `potency` (how strong the effect) and `keeping` (how well it stores) are the two things a luxury/boost system would plausibly read, and that system does not exist. Expect to re-author them - possibly to re-axis them entirely - when it does. AND GRAPE IS CURRENTLY DOMINATED ON BOTH AXES (0.20 / 0.15 against tea's 0.45 / 0.80 and tobacco's 0.85 / 0.75), which sits badly against this file's own 'there is no best material' principle. That is recorded honestly rather than resolved: a grape's whole value is on the far side of a craft (fermenting) that has not been built, so inventing a third axis today to make the roster look balanced would be inventing a number to fit a rule. See .claude/rules/core_sim/crafting.md. Each CRAFTED material has exactly ONE craft track (hide -> tanning, fibre -> weaving, bone -> bone_working, wood -> weaving), which is the knowledge half of the ladder: a band that lives by hunting learns tanning, a gathering band learns weaving, and a band that cannot reach bone never advances bone-working - specialisation emerges from where you are standing rather than from a tech menu. WHAT EACH PAIR OF AXES MEANS: hide is skin and pelt, where `toughness` is what a sled harness and a tent wall want and `suppleness` is what cordage, a bag and clothing want - THE canonical no-best-material pair. fibre is bast, sinew, grass and wool - anything twisted or woven - where `fineness` is how thin a thread it makes and `strength` is what that thread will hold; the two genuinely trade off, which is why flax and hay are not one thing. bone is antler, horn, tusk and long bone, where `density` is how hard it is and how well it holds a point and `length` is how big a piece the animal gives you, which is why a mammoth's is excellent and a hare's is barely a piece at all. wood is withy, bough and split timber, where `hardness` is what resists and holds an edge and `pliancy` is what bends and weaves without breaking - a genuinely opposed pair, since a hard wood will not bend into a hurdle and a pliant one splits into long lengths but takes no load; wood takes `hand_working` for the three organics' reason, because you can bend a withy by hand, and its craft is `weaving` rather than a minted wood_working because the hurdles recipe IS a weave and a new craft would need a discovery id, a lesson_costs entry and a bench tool that this roster does not have. hurdles are woven fence panels lashed with hide thong, where `stoutness` is how much a panel holds and `span` is how much ground it covers - opposed because a stout panel is heavy and short and a wide-spanning one is light. A MATERIAL'S OWN KEYS ARE CLOSED (deny_unknown_fields), so a mistyped `hand_workng` is a parse error rather than a material that silently stopped being workable; the prose therefore lives here at the file level, as it does in every other config in this directory.
